Wolfram FileExistsQ gave 'with ..: False  normalised: True  ParentDirectory form: True' for that clone, and True for all three in the 6-characters-shorter audit_verify_clone, where the run succeeded.

location: Line 1749ff, argument 4 ('A connected Lie group is generated by the exponentials of its Lie algebra (*cited*), so the exp(theta S^AB) generate the identity component'); argument preamble line ~142 ('pi(Gamma(v)) is the reflection in the hyperplane orthogonal to v (`finite_groups` computes it for v = e_A)')
problem: The Pin(4,4) argument says every claim is either a check, a proof given there, or a fact marked cited. Two steps are neither. (1) The cited fact (G_0 is generated by exp of the whole Lie algebra) is weaker than the step that uses it: that the 28 one-parameter groups exp(theta S^AB) of a basis generate Spin_0(4,4). That step needs 'coordinates of the second kind': the product map (t_1..t_28) -> prod exp(t_i S^i) covers a neighbourhood of I16, and a neighbourhood generates a connected group. (2) The reflection property of pi(Gamma(v)) for general v is used (Cartan-Dieudonne, transitivity) but is only computed for v = e_A. Both facts are true, so the conclusions stand; the write-up still states more than it proves or cites.
evidence: md line 147 (argument 4) and line 142 (notation paragraph), quoted above. finite_groups checks only the eight basis reflections ('Each Gamma_A acts (twisted) as the reflection diag(1, .., -1 at A, .., 1)').
fix: In argument 4, cite the standard fact actually used: products of the one-parameter subgroups of a basis cover a neighbourhood of the identity (inverse function theorem), and a neighbourhood generates a connected Lie group. In the preamble, add the one-line proof -Gamma(v) Gamma_C Gamma(v)^-1 = Gamma_C - 2 eta(v,e_C)/eta(v,v) Gamma(v), which follows from the Clifford relation, or mark it *cited*.
